review.notes: TRIAGE coverage: full-document machine scan of all 39 pages (code-fence balance, structure-inside-fences scan, normalized 4-gram page containment plus word-level missing-token diff against the extracted PDF text), then line-level manual inspection of every low-hit page (10-12, 14, 19-24, 30-39) and mid-hit pages 1, 8, 25, 26, 36. Rendered page-bottom crops of physical pages 1, 8 and 11 were visually read at 300 dpi to transcribe the dropped footnote bodies. Low 4-gram hit rates on pages 19-24 and 30 are LaTeX-equivalent math (OCR emits LaTeX, PDF text layer emits unicode), pages 32-38 are appendix prompt figures embedded as images whose printed text the containment scan cannot match, and pages 14/11 residual tokens are PDF text-layer table-cell artifacts (30RM@256, Maj@8), not droppage. Punctuation spacing after inline math is handled by the shared OCR normalizer. Figure 9 is present only as a transcribed code block (see unresolved); its in-block garbling is figure-internal text shown beside a caption and was not patched.

patches.before: The base models, instruct models, and reward model of the Qwen2.5-Math series are available on Hugging Face $^{1}$ and ModelScope $^{2}$ , and the evaluation scripts on GitHub $^{3}$ . We have also developed a demo that supports the TIR mode in Qwen-Agent $^{4}$ , which allows running code locally to experience Tool-Integrated Reasoning capabilities of Qwen2.5-Math.
patches.after:

unresolved.evidence: Figure 9 (the GaoKao Math Cloze prompt for base models) has no image embed in the OCR Markdown: its printed prompt content is transcribed into a fenced ```txt block that precedes the 'Figure 9:' caption, unlike Figures 5-8 and 10-13 which are embedded images. Cleanup patches cannot add image embeds (the exporter rejects changed embed sets), so restoring the embed requires regenerating the OCR source. The transcription block itself stays; some in-block prompt math is garbled OCR of figure text ('\ Newcastle', '\(left\{'), which is figure-internal text and not repaired here.

Figure 14 (the GaoKao multiple-choice prompt for instruct models) is represented as a flattened HTML table rather than an embedded image; the printed prompt text is present in the table, so no content is lost, but the representation differs from the other prompt figures. Same embed-immutability constraint as above.
